about: The fields of field guide 04 (rung R0b: tape-measure the robot with it switched off and unplugged). Ids are stable: the runner's typed measurement entry (unit R07, confirmation K9) is meant to use the same ids for every field marked measurement_entry. Every field is answered with a value or the word 'unknown'; there are no default values, and an empty line is not an answer.
frame: Body frame, seen from above: origin T = the point on the sheet under the centre of the collet; body axis = the robot's centre line, spindle at the front; 'back' = mm behind T along the axis (minus = ahead of T); 'right' = mm to the right of the axis, square to it (minus = left), right as seen standing behind the robot looking toward the spindle; angles at T from the backward axis, positive to the right.

units.deg: degrees; for footprint angles, positive toward the robot's right

fields.meaning: Date of the measurement session.
fields.how_measured: Written at the start (step 1).
fields.feeds: Recorded with every measured value (the measurement entry K9 records the time, design 7.4).

fields.meaning: Name or initials of the person who measured.
fields.how_measured: Written at the start (step 1).
fields.feeds: The measurement entry K9 records the operator's name with every value (design 7.4).

fields.meaning: Rear wheel module (spec 08 q1): how far its contact centre lies behind the collet mark T, along the body axis.
fields.how_measured: Square from the body axis to the q1 cross, distance from T to the foot of the square (step 6).
fields.feeds: Support point q1 as body-frame coordinates; cross-checks footprint.q1_mm and footprint.q1_deg (spec 08 §Footprint model; design 4.5 support distances and angles, 4.6 footprint models vendor / measured / union).

expected.source: derived from spec 08 §Footprint model at C = 0: q1 = p + (0, -402)

fields.meaning: Rear wheel module (q1): how far its contact centre lies to the right of the body axis (minus = left).
fields.how_measured: Length of the square's edge from the axis to the q1 cross, with a minus sign if the cross is left of the axis (step 6).
fields.feeds: Support point q1 as body-frame coordinates (spec 08 §Footprint model; design 4.6).

expected.source: derived from spec 08 §Footprint model: q1 lies on the body axis

fields.meaning: Rear wheel module (q1): straight distance from the collet mark T to its contact centre.
fields.how_measured: Tape from T to the q1 cross (step 6).
fields.feeds: Support distance r1 (spec 08 §Constants: rear support distance; design 4.5); R0b go criterion (design 11.2).

fields.meaning: Rear wheel module (q1): angle at T from the backward body axis to its contact centre, positive to the right.
fields.how_measured: arctan(footprint.q1_right_mm / footprint.q1_back_mm) on a calculator (step 6).
fields.feeds: Support angle delta1 (spec 08 §Footprint model; design 4.5); R0b go criterion (design 11.2).

expected.source: spec 08 §Footprint model (q1 along -u(theta)); go criterion design 11.2 R0b

fields.meaning: Right side wheel module (spec 08 q2): how far its contact centre lies behind T, along the body axis.
fields.how_measured: Distance from T to the point F where the body axis meets the line through the two side crosses (step 6).
fields.feeds: Support point q2 as body-frame coordinates; cross-checks footprint.q2_mm and footprint.q2_deg (spec 08 §Footprint model; design 4.6).

expected.source: derived from spec 08 §Footprint model at C = 0: q2 = p + (204.7, -51.0)

fields.meaning: Right side wheel module (q2): how far its contact centre lies to the right of the body axis.
fields.how_measured: Distance from F to the q2 cross along the line through the side crosses (step 6).
fields.feeds: Support point q2 as body-frame coordinates (spec 08 §Footprint model; design 4.6).

expected.source: derived from spec 08 §Footprint model at C = 0: q2 = p + (204.7, -51.0)

fields.meaning: Right side wheel module (q2): straight distance from T to its contact centre.
fields.how_measured: Tape from T to the q2 cross (step 6).
fields.feeds: Support distance r2 (spec 08 §Constants: side support distance; design 4.5); R0b go criterion (design 11.2).

fields.meaning: Right side wheel module (q2): angle at T from the backward body axis to its contact centre, positive to the right.
fields.how_measured: arctan(footprint.q2_right_mm / footprint.q2_back_mm) on a calculator (step 6).
fields.feeds: Support angle delta2 (spec 08 §Constants: side support angle +76 deg; design 4.5); R0b go criterion (design 11.2).

fields.meaning: Left side wheel module (spec 08 q3): how far its contact centre lies behind T, along the body axis.
fields.how_measured: The same distance T to F as for q2, because both side crosses lie on one line square to the axis (step 6).
fields.feeds: Support point q3 as body-frame coordinates; cross-checks footprint.q3_mm and footprint.q3_deg (spec 08 §Footprint model; design 4.6).

expected.source: derived from spec 08 §Footprint model at C = 0: q3 = p + (-204.7, -51.0)

fields.meaning: Left side wheel module (q3): how far its contact centre lies to the right of the body axis; it is on the left, so the value is negative.
fields.how_measured: Distance from F to the q3 cross along the line through the side crosses, written with a minus sign (step 6).
fields.feeds: Support point q3 as body-frame coordinates (spec 08 §Footprint model; design 4.6).

expected.source: derived from spec 08 §Footprint model at C = 0: q3 = p + (-204.7, -51.0)

fields.meaning: Left side wheel module (q3): straight distance from T to its contact centre.
fields.how_measured: Tape from T to the q3 cross (step 6).
fields.feeds: Support distance r3 (spec 08 §Constants: side support distance; design 4.5); R0b go criterion (design 11.2).

fields.meaning: Left side wheel module (q3): angle at T from the backward body axis to its contact centre; it is on the left, so the value is negative.
fields.how_measured: arctan(footprint.q3_right_mm / footprint.q3_back_mm) on a calculator, which comes out negative (step 6).
fields.feeds: Support angle delta3 (spec 08 §Constants: side support angle -76 deg; design 4.5); R0b go criterion (design 11.2).

fields.meaning: Straight distance between the contact centres of the rear (q1) and right (q2) modules.
fields.how_measured: Tape between the q1 and q2 crosses (step 6).
fields.feeds: Cross-check of the three support points (spec 08 §Footprint model: a nearly equilateral triangle with sides of about 406 to 410 mm).

expected.source: derived from spec 08 §Footprint model at C = 0

fields.meaning: Straight distance between the contact centres of the right (q2) and left (q3) modules.
fields.how_measured: Tape between the q2 and q3 crosses (step 6).
fields.feeds: Cross-check of the three support points (spec 08 §Footprint model).

expected.source: derived from spec 08 §Footprint model at C = 0

fields.meaning: Straight distance between the contact centres of the left (q3) and rear (q1) modules.
fields.how_measured: Tape between the q3 and q1 crosses (step 6).
fields.feeds: Cross-check of the three support points (spec 08 §Footprint model).

expected.source: derived from spec 08 §Footprint model at C = 0

fields.meaning: Does the body axis drawn on the sheet (square to the line through the side wheels, through T) run along the middle of the body outline, from the spindle end to the back?
fields.how_measured: Compare the drawn axis with the outline dots and the photo from above (step 6).
fields.feeds: Whether the drawn axis is the robot's forward direction, which spec 08 assumes for u(theta) (spec 08 §Caveats; U-20). 'no' or 'unknown' goes to design review.

fields.meaning: How the wheel contact centres were found: halfway between the marks of the module's outer roller faces (end_marks), or the middle of the carbon marks alone (middle_of_marks).
fields.how_measured: Recorded while marking the crosses (step 6).
fields.feeds: Provenance of the measured support points (design 3.1: measured facts carry how they were measured).

fields.meaning: Largest difference between the two runs for any of the footprint distances; 'unknown' if you measured only once.
fields.how_measured: Repeat steps 1 to 6 on a fresh sheet and compare (step 12).
fields.feeds: The tolerance recorded with the footprint values (K9 records a tolerance with every value, design 7.4).

fields.meaning: File names of the photos of the robot from above and of the finished sheet, each with a rule in the picture.
fields.how_measured: Photos taken in step 4 and step 6.
fields.feeds: Evidence for design review (U-22).

fields.meaning: Rear module (q1): how many separate wheels it has (a report speaks of nine wheels in three sets).
fields.how_measured: Count, looking at the module from the side and from below (step 7).
fields.feeds: Evidence for the wheel contact radius r_w and the omni-wheel model (PAR §4); design review.

fields.meaning: Rear module (q1): outer diameter of its wheel, over the rollers (the largest, if they differ).
fields.how_measured: Rule or callipers across the wheel at its widest (step 7).
fields.feeds: Evidence for r_w; design review (U-22).

fields.meaning: Rear module (q1): overall width along the wheel axle, from the outer face of the outermost roller on one side to the outer face of the outermost roller on the other side.
fields.how_measured: Rule or callipers on the module, cross-checked with the end marks on the sheet (step 7).
fields.feeds: Lower bound of the contact radius: half of it is the least wheel.q1.contact_radius_mm can be (design 4.5 r_w).

fields.meaning: Rear module (q1): number of rows of rollers across the whole module (all its wheels together).
fields.how_measured: Count, looking at the module from the side and from below (step 7).
fields.feeds: Evidence for r_w and the omni-wheel model ('two rollers are always in contact', PAR §4); design review.

fields.meaning: Rear module (q1): centre-to-centre distance between neighbouring roller rows along the axle (the largest, if uneven; 0 for a single row).
fields.how_measured: Rule or callipers between the middles of two neighbouring rows (step 7).
fields.feeds: Evidence for r_w; design review (U-22).

fields.meaning: Rear module (q1): the longest dimension of the area where it can touch the panel: the longest dimension of its still print, or the width of its widest rolling band measured across the direction of rolling, whichever is larger (a band's length only shows how far the robot was pushed).
fields.how_measured: Rule on the still print (step 2) and across the rolling bands (step 5), measured in step 7.
fields.feeds: Evidence for the wheel contact radius r_w (design 4.5; U-22).

fields.meaning: Rear module (q1): radius of the circle around its contact centre that holds every place where it can touch the panel: the largest of the distance from its cross to the outer edge of its still print, half the width of its widest rolling band, and half of wheel.q1.width_mm; rounded up.
fields.how_measured: Rule from the q1 cross to the edge of its still print (step 2), band widths (step 5) and the module width; the largest, rounded up (step 7).
fields.feeds: Wheel contact radius r_w (design 4.5: 40 mm DEFAULT_UNMEASURED until R0b; rho = r_w + m_w with m_w = 15 mm); the design uses one r_w for all wheels, so the largest of the three modules is the conservative value; every wheel-disc check (design 4.9) and the closed-profile limit of design 4.20.

fields.meaning: Right side module (q2): how many separate wheels it has.
fields.how_measured: Count, looking at the module from the side and from below (step 7).
fields.feeds: Evidence for r_w and the omni-wheel model (PAR §4); design review.

fields.meaning: Right side module (q2): outer diameter of its wheel, over the rollers (the largest, if they differ).
fields.how_measured: Rule or callipers across the wheel at its widest (step 7).
fields.feeds: Evidence for r_w; design review (U-22).

fields.meaning: Right side module (q2): overall width along the wheel axle, outer roller face to outer roller face.
fields.how_measured: Rule or callipers on the module, cross-checked with the end marks on the sheet (step 7).
fields.feeds: Lower bound of the contact radius: half of it is the least wheel.q2.contact_radius_mm can be (design 4.5 r_w).

fields.meaning: Right side module (q2): number of rows of rollers across the whole module.
fields.how_measured: Count, looking at the module from the side and from below (step 7).
fields.feeds: Evidence for r_w and the omni-wheel model (PAR §4); design review.

fields.meaning: Right side module (q2): centre-to-centre distance between neighbouring roller rows along the axle (the largest, if uneven; 0 for a single row).
fields.how_measured: Rule or callipers between the middles of two neighbouring rows (step 7).
fields.feeds: Evidence for r_w; design review (U-22).

fields.meaning: Right side module (q2): the longest dimension of the area where it can touch the panel: the longest dimension of its still print, or the width of its widest rolling band measured across the direction of rolling, whichever is larger (a band's length only shows how far the robot was pushed).
fields.how_measured: Rule on the still print (step 2) and across the rolling bands (step 5), measured in step 7.
fields.feeds: Evidence for the wheel contact radius r_w (design 4.5; U-22).

fields.meaning: Right side module (q2): radius of the circle around its contact centre that holds every place where it can touch the panel: the largest of the distance from its cross to the outer edge of its still print, half the width of its widest rolling band, and half of wheel.q2.width_mm; rounded up.
fields.how_measured: Rule from the q2 cross to the edge of its still print (step 2), band widths (step 5) and the module width; the largest, rounded up (step 7).
fields.feeds: Wheel contact radius r_w (design 4.5: 40 mm DEFAULT_UNMEASURED until R0b; rho = r_w + 15 mm); the largest of the three modules is the conservative value; every wheel-disc check (design 4.9) and the closed-profile limit of design 4.20.

fields.meaning: Left side module (q3): how many separate wheels it has.
fields.how_measured: Count, looking at the module from the side and from below (step 7).
fields.feeds: Evidence for r_w and the omni-wheel model (PAR §4); design review.

fields.meaning: Left side module (q3): outer diameter of its wheel, over the rollers (the largest, if they differ).
fields.how_measured: Rule or callipers across the wheel at its widest (step 7).
fields.feeds: Evidence for r_w; design review (U-22).

fields.meaning: Left side module (q3): overall width along the wheel axle, outer roller face to outer roller face.
fields.how_measured: Rule or callipers on the module, cross-checked with the end marks on the sheet (step 7).
fields.feeds: Lower bound of the contact radius: half of it is the least wheel.q3.contact_radius_mm can be (design 4.5 r_w).

fields.meaning: Left side module (q3): number of rows of rollers across the whole module.
fields.how_measured: Count, looking at the module from the side and from below (step 7).
fields.feeds: Evidence for r_w and the omni-wheel model (PAR §4); design review.

fields.meaning: Left side module (q3): centre-to-centre distance between neighbouring roller rows along the axle (the largest, if uneven; 0 for a single row).
fields.how_measured: Rule or callipers between the middles of two neighbouring rows (step 7).
fields.feeds: Evidence for r_w; design review (U-22).

fields.meaning: Left side module (q3): the longest dimension of the area where it can touch the panel: the longest dimension of its still print, or the width of its widest rolling band measured across the direction of rolling, whichever is larger (a band's length only shows how far the robot was pushed).
fields.how_measured: Rule on the still print (step 2) and across the rolling bands (step 5), measured in step 7.
fields.feeds: Evidence for the wheel contact radius r_w (design 4.5; U-22).

fields.meaning: Left side module (q3): radius of the circle around its contact centre that holds every place where it can touch the panel: the largest of the distance from its cross to the outer edge of its still print, half the width of its widest rolling band, and half of wheel.q3.width_mm; rounded up.
fields.how_measured: Rule from the q3 cross to the edge of its still print (step 2), band widths (step 5) and the module width; the largest, rounded up (step 7).
fields.feeds: Wheel contact radius r_w (design 4.5: 40 mm DEFAULT_UNMEASURED until R0b; rho = r_w + 15 mm); the largest of the three modules is the conservative value; every wheel-disc check (design 4.9) and the closed-profile limit of design 4.20.

fields.meaning: Does the switched-off, unplugged robot roll when pushed gently by hand? 'yes' means the rolling bands were made; 'unknown' means it was not tried.
fields.how_measured: A gentle push by the body; never forced (step 5).
fields.feeds: Provenance of the contact extent and radius: without rolling bands they come from the still prints and the module width only (U-22).

fields.meaning: File names of the photos of each wheel module (side and, if you can see it, from below) and of the carbon marks, with a rule in the picture.
fields.how_measured: Photos taken in step 7.
fields.feeds: Evidence for design review (U-22).

fields.meaning: Anything about the wheels that the fields do not capture, for example wheels of one module that do not share an axle, an end that could not be reached with the square, or worn or damaged rollers.
fields.how_measured: Written during step 7.
fields.feeds: Design review (U-22).

fields.meaning: How far the body outline reaches ahead of T (toward the front), along the body axis.
fields.how_measured: Square from the axis to the front-most outline dot, distance from T to the foot (step 8).
fields.feeds: Body hull (design 4.5: the hull of the wheel discs + 60 mm, DEFAULT_UNMEASURED); B-TOWER and, until the wire attachment is measured, P-REACH (design 4.6, 4.9).

fields.meaning: How far the body outline reaches behind T, along the body axis.
fields.how_measured: Square from the axis to the rear-most outline dot, distance from T to the foot (step 8).
fields.feeds: Body hull (design 4.5); B-TOWER, P-REACH (design 4.6, 4.9).

fields.meaning: How far the body outline reaches to the left of the body axis, measured square to it (a positive number).
fields.how_measured: Square from the axis to the left-most outline dot (step 8).
fields.feeds: Body hull (design 4.5); B-TOWER, P-REACH (design 4.6, 4.9).

fields.meaning: How far the body outline reaches to the right of the body axis, measured square to it (a positive number).
fields.how_measured: Square from the axis to the right-most outline dot (step 8).
fields.feeds: Body hull (design 4.5); B-TOWER, P-REACH (design 4.6, 4.9).

fields.meaning: The largest straight distance from T to any point of the body outline.
fields.how_measured: Tape from T to the few outline dots that look farthest; the largest (step 8).
fields.feeds: Body hull bound when the body turns about the tool (design 4.8 body hull bound, 4.5); B-TOWER.

fields.meaning: Optional: the outline as a list of back,right pairs in mm in the body frame, going round the body, for example '-60,0; -40,150; ...'. The photo of the sheet is enough for now.
fields.how_measured: Square and tape from the axis to each outline dot (step 8).
fields.feeds: A body hull polygon instead of the bounding box (design 4.5 body hull).

fields.meaning: File names of the photos from directly above with a rule, and of the traced outline on the sheet.
fields.how_measured: Photos taken in step 4 and step 8.
fields.feeds: Evidence for design review (U-22).

fields.meaning: Where the towers' measuring wires attach to the robot: directly above the collet (W within 2 mm of T on the sheet), somewhere else on the robot, or no attachment point found.
fields.how_measured: Inspection from outside and the W mark on the sheet (step 4, step 9).
fields.feeds: Wire attachment (design 4.5: unmeasured = anywhere on the body hull; machine.toml holds it as an offset from the tool in the body frame); P-REACH uses the tool point only if it is on the spindle axis (design 4.6, 4.9).

fields.meaning: Does the part the wires attach to turn freely about a vertical axis relative to the body (swivel), or not (fixed)?
fields.how_measured: Turn it gently by hand, never forced, wires not pulled (step 9).
fields.feeds: How far the body may turn while tethered: the design keeps the net rotation within +-350 deg of the start heading until R0b shows how the wires attach (design 4.10.2, U-49).

fields.meaning: Do both towers' wires attach at the same point? If not, describe both points in wire.notes; that case goes to design review.
fields.how_measured: Inspection from outside (step 9).
fields.feeds: P-REACH model of the attachment (design 4.6; U-49).

fields.meaning: How far the wire attachment point (projected straight down, mark W) lies behind T along the body axis (minus = ahead of T).
fields.how_measured: Square from the axis to W, distance from T to the foot (step 6, step 9).
fields.feeds: Wire attachment offset from the tool in the body frame (unit P01 machine.toml); P-REACH (design 4.6, 4.9).

fields.meaning: How far the wire attachment point (mark W) lies to the right of the body axis (minus = left).
fields.how_measured: Length of the square's edge from the axis to W, minus if left (step 6, step 9).
fields.feeds: Wire attachment offset from the tool in the body frame (unit P01 machine.toml); P-REACH (design 4.6, 4.9).

fields.meaning: Optional: height of the wire attachment point above the surface the robot stands on.
fields.how_measured: Tape held vertical next to the robot (step 9).
fields.feeds: Not used by the current checks; recorded for the design review of P-REACH (U-49).

fields.meaning: File names of the photos of the wire attachment: from the side, from above and close up, with a rule in the picture.
fields.how_measured: Photos taken in step 9.
fields.feeds: Evidence for design review (U-49).

fields.meaning: How the wires attach (for example magnetic, a clip), anything that limits how far the body can turn, and the second point if the wires attach at two points.
fields.how_measured: Written during step 9.
fields.feeds: Design review (U-49).

fields.meaning: Overall length of a tower's base, the part that stands on the panel or beside it (the larger tower if the two differ).
fields.how_measured: Rule or tape on the base (step 10).
fields.feeds: Tower base keep-out (design 4.5: a disc of 120 mm radius at each tower, DEFAULT_UNMEASURED); B-TOWER and T-TOWER (design 4.9).

fields.meaning: Overall width of a tower's base, square to its length (the larger tower if the two differ).
fields.how_measured: Rule or tape on the base (step 10).
fields.feeds: Tower base keep-out (design 4.5); B-TOWER and T-TOWER (design 4.9).

fields.meaning: Largest distance from the point straight below where the wire leaves the tower to the outer edge of its base (the larger tower if the two differ).
fields.how_measured: Square and rule on the base (step 10).
fields.feeds: Radius of the tower base keep-out disc (design 4.5: 120 mm DEFAULT_UNMEASURED); B-TOWER and T-TOWER (design 4.9).

fields.meaning: File names of the photos of each tower from above and from the side, with a rule in the picture.
fields.how_measured: Photos taken in step 10.
fields.feeds: Evidence for design review (Q5).

fields.meaning: What you will use to stop the robot in an emergency (the physical stop).
fields.how_measured: Inspection from outside, robot unplugged (step 11).
fields.feeds: Fact stop.kind (design 11.2 R0b); the ARM confirmation K5 names it (design 7.4); U-25.

fields.meaning: Where the physical stop is, in words (for example 'red button on the back of the robot, left of the handle').
fields.how_measured: Inspection (step 11).
fields.feeds: The text of the ARM confirmation K5 (design 7.4); U-25.

fields.meaning: Does the stop stay off once pressed until you deliberately reset it (twist or pull)?
fields.how_measured: Press and reset it with the robot unplugged, which is harmless (step 11).
fields.feeds: The stop drill of R2 and R3b (design 11.2); U-25.

fields.meaning: What the stop switches off: the controller's power (everything, including Wi-Fi), only the motors and the spindle, or only the spindle.
fields.how_measured: From a label, the manual or your experience, never by opening the housing; rung R2 checks it with power (step 11).
fields.feeds: Whether pressing the stop also counts as a power cycle (it does not if it cuts only motors or spindle: K6, design 7.4, 7.7); U-25.

fields.meaning: How you know what the stop switches off.
fields.how_measured: Recorded with stop.cuts (step 11).
fields.feeds: Provenance of stop.cuts until R2 has checked it with power (design 3.1, 11.2).

fields.meaning: Which switch turns the robot's controller (its electronics and Wi-Fi) off, and where it is; it may be the same as the stop.
fields.how_measured: Inspection and the manual, robot unplugged (step 11).
fields.feeds: The power-cycle confirmation K6: 'the switch named in Q7, not only an e-stop that cuts motors or spindle' (design 7.4, 7.7).

fields.meaning: Does the router (the spindle motor) have its own on/off switch?
fields.how_measured: Inspection from outside (step 11).
fields.feeds: The motion rungs keep the router's own switch off where it has one (R3, design 11.2; U-17).

fields.meaning: Where the router's own switch is, in words; 'none' if it has none.
fields.how_measured: Inspection (step 11).
fields.feeds: Rung procedures R3 and R4 (design 11.2; U-17).

fields.meaning: Optional: how many seconds the router takes to stop turning after its power is cut, if you know it; 'unknown' otherwise. Nothing is switched on to find out.
fields.how_measured: From experience or the manual (step 11).
fields.feeds: The stop drills and the ARM text (Q7; U-25).

fields.meaning: How you know spindle.rundown_s.
fields.how_measured: Recorded with spindle.rundown_s (step 11).
fields.feeds: Provenance of spindle.rundown_s (design 3.1).

fields.meaning: Anything unexpected, and anything you could not measure and why.
fields.how_measured: Written at the end (step 13).
fields.feeds: Design review.
